Subject: Cost-Minimizing FY Coverage Mix to Meet Our Service Commitments

Team,

We’re preparing our FY plan to meet a dozen service commitments at the lowest possible total spend. Each program below can be dialed up or down within its operating window, and each one contributes in specific ways to our required coverage, quality, and compliance metrics. Our goal is to minimize the overall budget while meeting or exceeding every commitment described at the end of this note.

For consistency, please treat one “unit” as a standardized block of effort (e.g., roughly a thousand staff-hours or its equivalent). Unless noted otherwise, units can be scheduled fractionally; where we require whole units, I’ve called that out. All programs are optional (we can choose zero) but each has an upper cap based on capacity or vendor limits.

Levers we can pull

- Rapid Response Vans
  • Unit cost: 1.18 per standardized unit of effort.
  • Deployment window: up to 12.82 units (can be fractional).
  • Impact: contributes 5.74 units to Safety Inspections Completed for every unit we deploy, and 8.24 units to the Customer Responsiveness Index per unit.

- Union Overtime Shifts
  • Unit cost: 7.37 per unit.
  • Deployment window: up to 14.85 units, in whole-unit increments (no partial shifts).
  • Impact: each unit delivers 7.26 units toward Urban Core Responses; 0.79 units for Priority Cases Resolved; 2.78 units for Training Hours Delivered; 6.53 units for Community Engagement Sessions; 0.63 units to the Customer Responsiveness Index; and 3.75 units for Aftercare Cases Closed.

- Tier-2 Contractor Blocks
  • Unit cost: 2.35 per unit.
  • Deployment window: up to 13.77 units (fractional allowed).
  • Impact: each unit adds 2.85 units to Urban Core Responses; 3.47 units to Suburban Preventive Checks; 8.08 units to Priority Cases Resolved; 6.07 units to Safety Inspections Completed; 5.29 units to Rural Miles Patrolled; 5.71 units to the Customer Responsiveness Index; and 9.11 units to Maintenance Backlog Cleared.

- Specialist Inspection Crews
  • Unit cost: 2.67 per unit.
  • Deployment window: up to 7.66 units (fractional allowed).
  • Impact: each unit contributes 8.82 units to Suburban Preventive Checks; 1.90 units to Safety Inspections Completed; 9.80 units to Training Hours Delivered; and 9.78 units to Night and Weekend Coverage.

Market limits and required minimums

To be compliant and maintain service levels, our plan must meet or exceed the following aggregate minimums across all deployed programs:
- Urban Core Responses: at least 142.33 units.
- Suburban Preventive Checks: at least 145.89 units.
- Priority Cases Resolved: at least 173.47 units.

- Emergency Drill Hours: at least 146.35 units.
- Aftercare Cases Closed: at least 102.03 units.

Please use this as the basis to produce a lowest-cost mix that respects the whole-unit requirements for Union Overtime Shifts and Seasonal Temp Crews, stays within every program’s cap, and clears every minimum above. Once we see the recommended mix, we’ll review sensitivity to small changes in the caps and the required minimums.
